B: Hiya mate! How you doing? Craig.
A: Hi. Tomasz. I'm fine.
B: Nice one. Where you based, Tomasz?
A: Walthamstow. East London.
B: London, lovely. I'm Cottingham, just outside Hull. Saw a hi-vis on your chair in the photo, so I thought, he's a worker, him. What do you do?
A: Electrician. Domestic, some light commercial.
B: Oh, brilliant. I'm a process operator on a chemical plant, so we've got the sparkies on site all the time. Permit-to-work, isolations, all that. Do you do much of that side?
A: Isolations, yes, every job. Lock off, test it's dead, then work. Some people skip testing. That's how people get hurt.
B: Spot on, mate. I say that to the young lads on shift. Don't assume, check. Takes two minutes. Sorry, can I ask you something electrical, actually? Cheeky one.
A: Yes, okay.
B: I've got a summerhouse in the garden I've been nearly finishing for two years. Rachel, my wife, has given up on it. I want lights and a couple of sockets in it. Can I just run an extension lead out from the kitchen?
A: No. Not long term. It should be a proper armoured cable, buried, from the consumer unit, with its own RCD protection. And it's notifiable, so you need a registered electrician to sign it off.
B: Right. So that's a no, then.
A: It's a no. An extension lead outside, with rain, it's not safe. Also for insurance.
B: Fair enough, I'll stop telling Rachel it's nearly done. What do you do outside of work?
A: Cycling, mostly. Weekends. Epping Forest, the Lea Valley.
B: Oh, the Strava map on your fridge! I clocked that. How far do you go?
A: Depends. Sixty, eighty kilometres. Sometimes a hundred, in summer.
B: A hundred! I do the odd parkrun at East Park and I'm stood at the finish chatting to anyone who'll listen, cos I'm not fast, so. Five-a-side as well when shifts let me. Knee's not great, rugby did that.
A: Cycling is better for knees, I think. Less impact.
B: That's what everyone tells me. Are you from round London originally, or?
A: Poland. Lublin.
B: Oh, Poland! I've been to Krakow. Stag do. Absolute carnage, but lovely city, honestly, the old square, the food. We had a proper night. Is Lublin near there?
A: Not so near. Maybe three, four hours. Lublin is more east. Smaller, but also an old town.
B: I'd go. You go back much?
A: Twice a year. My parents are there. My dad still works, he's nearly sixty. His back is bad.
B: Ah, that's hard, mate, being far away from that. My dad had a stroke last year, and I'm half an hour away and I still feel like I'm not doing enough. Must be harder from London.
A: Yeah. It is. I call every week.
B: That's all you can do, isn't it. Sorry, I've gone off on one, I do that. How long have you been
